text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey and Israel sign a new deal for military cooperation which boosts ties with the Turkish Cypriot pseudostate in the north.
- Doctors and nurses strike will cripple hospitals for four hours today.
- Three foreign banks withdraw from a Cypriot investment scheme at Krasnodar on the Black Sea.

- The United States is seeking small-scale confidence building measures between the two sides to reduce tension in Cyprus - but rules out a package deal settling the Cyprus problem and Greco-Turkish disputes.
- Intense diplomatic efforts start with the two sides to accept an extension of the unmanning agreement.
- "They are stealing our bread and butter." Workers threaten to strike at hotels employing foreigners.
- Thousands of offshore companies can register on the Cyprus Stock Exchange after the approval of regulations.
- United Nations soldiers arrested Greek Cypriots close to Nicosia airport while carrying out work for the National Guard.
- Britain pushes for direct talks between the two sides, linking it to Cyprus's accession talks due to start with the EU.
- Disy party leader Yiannakis Matsis goes to London today for by-pass surgery.
